Elon Musk and SpaceX announced a pledge to donate two shares of company stock to every child in the United States. The shares will be deposited into active Trump Accounts, which are tax-advantaged investment accounts created under a 2025 tax law. The initial giveaway is valued at approximately eighteen billion dollars based on recent stock prices, involving an eligible population of seventy to seventy-two million children. SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell separately pledged more than two million shares of stock. Musk subsequently stated on social media that he will donate his portion of the shares directly.

Justice Patricia Nyaundi ordered Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale to disclose all agreements with the United States within forty-five days and barred further construction or operations at the fifty-bed site. The project formed part of a planned thirteen point five million dollar United States initiative for Kenya. Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo have surpassed twelve thousand with over five thousand nine hundred deaths.

Ukrainian sea drones attacked and damaged a Russian naval corvette named Merkury and a cargo vessel named MV Angara near the eastern Libyan port of Benghazi. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that Ukrainian forces carried out the operation. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha stated that the military action was directed against Moscow and not against Libya. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed concern that the war could expand into the Mediterranean. Two Libyan soldiers were killed in the strikes according to regional reports.

President Donald Trump demanded an immediate federal investigation into the Commerce Department after its Bureau of Economic Analysis revised third-quarter annualized gross domestic product growth up from three point four percent to four point three percent. Trump claimed on social media that the initial pre-election estimate was a massive error intended to affect the midterm elections, in which Republican candidates suffered heavy losses. Historical data shows that nine-tenths of a percentage point revisions have occurred previously in routine estimation stages.

A high-speed passenger ferry traveling from Hong Kong's Sheung Wan to Shenzhen collided with a floating dry dock near the Tsing Yi oil depot, injuring twenty-two people. Preliminary reports indicated that the ferry captain lost control after the helm malfunctioned. Emergency responders deployed fifteen ambulances along with firefighting vessels and mobile casualty units to the scene.

Myanmar military-backed leader Min Aung Hlaing stated that his government will refuse to comply with parts of the international court ruling that held the country responsible for genocide against the Rohingya minority. Speaking at a Cabinet meeting reported by state media, the leader described the case as a one-sided accusation and asserted that the term has damaged the nation's reputation. The court ordered the government to prevent further violations, though the decision carries no direct enforcement mechanism beyond reporting noncompliance to the United Nations Security Council.

Danish referee Morten Krogh halted proceedings and sent both teams to the dressing rooms after supporters displayed a banner reading revolt against the occupation and freedom for Palestine, waved Palestinian flags, and chanted anti-Israel slogans. Georgia's interior ministry stated that violent actions and physical clashes began before the flags were displayed during the march to the stadium. Georgian authorities detained sixteen individuals and reported three injured police officers before Besiktas won the match two to one.

United States President Donald Trump stated at his Mar-a-Lago estate that he had reviewed sufficient information to conclude Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang does not pose a security threat. Trump described his administration's behind-the-scenes intervention to reinstate Huang as a major benefit for the world and the United States. Huang resigned on November twelfth from Nvidia following revelations of an extramarital affair with an executive linked to Chinese intelligence, which triggered internal administration friction and classified memos from Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Nvidia's board of directors subsequently reinstated Huang following the administration push, leading to a partial stock price rebound.

European Union leaders meeting at a Brussels summit agreed to nominate former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernandez de Cos as the next president of the European Central Bank, succeeding Christine Lagarde when her term ends on February seventh, 2027. Hernandez de Cos, currently the general manager of the Bank for International Settlements, secured the role after the Netherlands withdrew support for its candidate, former Dutch central bank head Klaas Knot. The nomination was part of a broader package deal involving executive board appointments negotiated by France and Germany. Financial analysts characterize Hernandez de Cos as a monetary policy dove compared to his rival.

United States presidential envoy Jared Kushner praised Russian President Vladimir Putin as a grandmaster of politics during an interview with Mathias Dopfner, chief executive of Axel Springer. Kushner stated that Putin has shown restraint by not using nuclear weapons in the conflict in Ukraine and has reassured American negotiators that using them is not his intention. Kushner and fellow presidential envoy Steve Witkoff held talks in Moscow and St Petersburg as part of ongoing diplomatic efforts. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky compared Donald Trump's relationship with Putin to befriending Adolf Hitler in response to the diplomatic evaluations.

## OPINION | Courts Cannot Substitute for Diplomacy in Public Health
A: This is Void Opinion. Through a pragmatic lens today. Courts cannot substitute for diplomacy in public health.
A: Fighting in eastern Congo has disrupted health response operations and forced the evacuation of medical workers. These numbers describe an unfolding epidemiological emergency of continental scale that requires cross-border infrastructure and rapid regional containment.
A: We observe a recurring institutional failure where urgent international health interventions collide with domestic legal mandates. When foreign security and medical arrangements bypass local consultation, the resulting backlash destroys the very stability the projects aim to secure. Public participation requirements exist precisely to prevent executive overreach during crises. Yet judicial intervention halting medical infrastructure in the middle of a regional outbreak creates its own severe hazard.
A: We must weigh the necessity of transparent governance against the brutal mathematics of pathogen transmission. The court correctly identified an illegal evasion of domestic statute by officials who traded procedural legitimacy for speed. At the same time, freezing a fifty-bed quarantine unit leaves the region structurally unprepared for a disease crossing borders with impunity. Foreign partners cannot impose medical installations from above without breeding immediate civil unrest. Host governments cannot ignore their own constitutional frameworks simply because a disease carries a high mortality rate.
A: Pragmatic health policy demands that we hold both truths simultaneously. Executive secrecy invites the exact populist resistance that halts critical containment work. Courts must enforce constitutional boundaries, but public health authorities must build local consent before breaking ground on containment zones. We find ourselves trapped between the danger of unchecked foreign medical outposts and the paralysis of administrative law. The path forward requires integrating transparency into emergency planning from the outset. Until we learn that legal compliance is a prerequisite for effective containment rather than an obstacle to it, every health crisis will trigger a crisis.

Fighting in eastern Congo has disrupted health response operations and forced the evacuation of medical workers. These numbers describe an unfolding epidemiological emergency of continental scale that requires cross-border infrastructure and rapid regional containment.
